headline: After Isaias: Panhandle waters still in recovery
dateline: Since Oct 9 · Pensacola to Port St. Joe · GIWW miles 167–376
what: Isaias came ashore near Destin as a Category 2. The Coast Guard put Pensacola, Destin, Panama City, Port St. Joe and GIWW miles 167–376 in recovery status, restricting boats 65 ft and over.
why: Channels are still being surveyed, marks may be off station and debris is in the water. Destin Marina took heavy damage.
todo: Check navcen.uscg.gov/port-status or call Sector Mobile at 251-266-5888 before you go. Daylight only, with a bow lookout.
source: U.S. Coast Guard via Baird Maritime

headline: Mobile, Gulfport, Pascagoula ports back open
dateline: Mobile normal Oct 10 · Pensacola & Panama City open Oct 12
what: Mobile returned to normal port condition at 4pm Saturday. The Coast Guard now lists Gulfport, Mobile, Pascagoula, Pensacola and Panama City as open.
why: The big harbors west of Destin are usable again, a good place to stage while the eastern Panhandle recovers.
todo: Read Coast Guard MSIB 136-26 for leftover limits, and call your marina first. Power and fuel may still be spotty.

tag: Grand Lagoon, Panama City Beach, FL
headline: PCB Seafood Festival is back on, this weekend
what: Moved from last weekend because of Isaias. Fri 5–9pm, Sat and Sun 11am–9pm. Free admission.
why: A waterfront festival right on Grand Lagoon, with fireworks over the lagoon Saturday at 9pm.
todo: Coming by boat? Call ahead for a slip. Panama City saw about 5.5 ft of surge, so some docks may be short on power.
